summary: Read-only audit of three untouched game areas, each finding adversarially verified against the code

confirmed.title: ESC and TAB do nothing on the end of raid card
confirmed.where: raidKey, the pause toggle near line 11124 (backOut's raid branch near 30955 also skips it)
confirmed.steps:
1. Extract, die, or abandon a run where you fired at least one shot. That skips the instant-quit branch, so the EXTRACTED / KILLED / ABANDONED card comes up.
2. Press ESC or TAB. Nothing happens.

Why: the card is an .outcome, not a .modal, so the document capture handler (escCloseTopModal) never sees it. state is still 'raid' and G.over is set, so this line and backOut's `if(G&&!G.over)` branch both skip. TAB is also in raidKey's preventDefault list, so it does not even move focus to the button.

The only ways out are the mouse on Log run and return, or controller B, which padMenu's /return/ search presses (v15.57). This breaks his Q1 rule (every menu closes on ESC) and the TAB card line that TAB "closes whatever is in front".
confirmed.test:
Setup, inside the closure on the dry fixture:
1. Start a raid on the play path.
2. Set G.tel.shots=1 so the instant-quit branch is skipped, then call endRaid('abandon').
3. Click the 'Too dark' tag and set #oc_note to 'zq-tab-probe-7'.
4. Dispatch new KeyboardEvent('keydown',{code:'Tab',key:'Tab'}) at window.

Expect all of these:
- #outcome is not .on
- state==='hub'
- pendingRun===null
- committedRun.note==='zq-tab-probe-7'
- committedRun.tags contains 'Too dark'

The note and tag prove the key went through ocCommit, not a class strip. On the current build #outcome stays .on, state is 'raid' and pendingRun is still set, so it fails.

Control: same setup, then oc_btn.click(). It must write the same committedRun fields and grow P.log by exactly one, so the key path logs once, like the click.

Use Tab for the main assertion, because a synthetic ESC runs late. Run Escape as a second arm after an await.

verdict.reason:
The bug is real. I traced every step in the current file.

1. The card is `<div class="outcome" id="outcome">`, not a .modal. It goes up at the end of endRaid (`document.getElementById('outcome').classList.add('on');`). endRaid first sets `G.over=how;` and shuts the pause box with `togglePauseBox(false);`. Nothing changes `state`, which stays 'raid' until oc_btn's onclick calls `showScreen('hub')`.

2. ESC goes through four listeners and none of them acts:
   - The window capture listener only acts when the pausebox is on.
   - The document capture listener returns at `var open=document.querySelectorAll('.modal.on'); if(!open.length) return;`.
   - The .imenu listener returns because no menu is open.
   - The main window listener passes `if(state!=='raid') return;` and calls raidKey.

3. Inside raidKey, every Escape or Tab branch needs !G.over, so none of them fires:
   - the emote-bar branch `if(G&&!G.over&&!G.trade&&G.emoteBar)`
   - the trade branch `if(G&&!G.over&&G.trade)`
   - the map/backpack branch `if((code==='Escape'||code==='Tab')&&G&&!G.over&&!pauseOpen&&(G.mapOpen||G.bagOpen)&&!repeat)`
   - the pause toggle `if((code==='Escape'||code==='KeyP'||code==='Tab')&&!repeat&&G&&!G.over)`

   Tab is also in the preventDefault list, so it cannot move focus to the button.

4. TAB also goes through backOut first (`if(e.code==='Tab'&&!pauseOpen&&!e.repeat){ if(backOut()) ...`). backOut returns false: there is no .imenu, escCloseTopModal finds no .modal.on, and its raid part sits behind `if(G&&!G.over)`.

5. Only the pad was fixed. padPanel's v15.57 comment says the card "is an .outcome, not a .modal". The keyboard never got the same fix.

6. No comment or ruling says ESC should be ignored on the card. The WHATSNEW line says TAB "closes whatever is in front", and the backOut and escCloseTopModal comments say every window is closed through its own door.

The proposed fix is sound:
- It goes before the pause toggle and after the `pauseOpen` gate, which lets Escape and Tab through. At that point nothing earlier has answered the key.
- It checks that the card is actually `.on`, so a G.over frame without the card is untouched.
- It needs a fresh press (`!repeat`).
- It presses oc_btn, whose onclick runs `ocCommit(); ... G=null; keys={}; showScreen('hub');`. That logs the run exactly as a click does, and `return` stops raidKey touching G after it has been nulled.
- `if(ev)` handles pad calls, where ev is null.
- No player text, number or seeded draw changes, and it touches no TXSHIP key.

One small gap: a press while the card's note textarea has focus is still dropped by the main listener's TEXTAREA bail-out. That matches how every other window behaves, so it needs no change.

confirmed.title: Backing out of the ascent kit question drops you on the bare floor, not back on the sector page
confirmed.where: askKit, near line 29337 (raised by the #sectordeploy handler near line 35351)
confirmed.steps:
1. At the lift, press E. The sector page opens.
2. Pick NIGHT and a weather, then press ASCEND TO THIS SECTOR. The #sectordeploy handler removes the sector page and calls askKit.
3. Press ESC, TAB, controller B or Not yet on 'What are you taking up?'.

Result: askno runs askRestore, but ASKBACK is null, so you land on the bare floor. To get back you must walk to the lift and press E again, which runs liftResetDay() and puts the surface back to DAY.

The v12.68 rule is that a question raised over a window returns to that window when closed. The Hire nobody question follows it (ASKBACK='tradermodal'). The kit question never sets ASKBACK.
confirmed.fix:
Insert this line immediately before openModal('askmodal'); in askKit:

  ASKBACK='sectormodal';   // backing out of the question returns to the sector page it was asked from

MY LOADOUT and FREEBIE KIT still ascend. askRestore runs before their callbacks, and ascendNow removes #sectormodal before startRaid.
confirmed.test:
Inside the closure, on the floor:
1. Call the lift station's act: HB.stations entry with id 'lift', .acts.KeyE[1]().
2. Click #condnight, then click #sectordeploy. Now #askmodal is .on and #sectormodal is not.
3. Dispatch keydown Tab at window.
4. Expect #askmodal off, #sectormodal .on, and P.cond==='night'. The current build leaves #sectormodal off, so it fails.

Control A: stage P.merc to a hired id, open the trader, click #mercclear, then Tab. It returns to #tradermodal on both builds. This proves the restore works and that only the kit question skips it.

Control B, after the fix: repeat the setup, click #askyes. Expect state==='raid' and #sectormodal not .on. End the raid in finally.

verdict.reason:
I could not refute it. Every step checks out in the current code.

1. The kit question is raised only from the sector page. The only caller of askKit is `document.getElementById('sectordeploy').onclick`. That handler runs `document.getElementById('sectormodal').classList.remove('on'); askKit();`.
2. askKit then calls `openModal('askmodal');`. openModal also strips `.on` from every other modal except tunemodal and simmodal. askKit never assigns ASKBACK. The only assignments in the file are `ASKBACK='tradermodal';` in the #mercclear handler, plus the declaration and the reset inside askRestore.
3. All three ways out end at #askno:
   - ESC and TAB go through the capture keydown handler to `escCloseTopModal();`.
   - TAB and controller B also go through `if(backOut()){...}`, and backOut calls escCloseTopModal.
   - askmodal has no data-esc button and no button whose id starts with "close", so escCloseTopModal falls through to `m.querySelector('#askno')` and clicks it.
4. The #askno handler runs `askRestore();`. askRestore starts with `if(!ASKBACK) return;`, so nothing is restored and he is left on the bare floor.
5. Getting back means pressing E at the lift again. That act runs `liftResetDay();   // v12.61` before `renderSector(); openModal('sectormodal');`, and liftResetDay sets `P.cond='day'`, so the NIGHT pick is lost.

This breaks the v12.68 rule written above `var ASKYES=null, ASKALT=null, ASKBACK=null;`: a card that closes the window it asks about names that window to restore. No comment or ruling exempts the kit question. It is not balance, and no player text changes.

The proposed fix is safe:
- On #askyes and #askalt, askRestore runs before the callback.
- MY LOADOUT and FREEBIE KIT both end in ascendNow, which runs `var sc=document.getElementById('sectormodal'); if(sc) sc.classList.remove('on');` before `startRaid()`, so the restored page cannot remain open over the raid.
- askRestore clears ASKBACK on every answer, so nothing stale is left behind.

The proposed line is correct as written.

confirmed.title: With Shift still held after stamina runs out, C does nothing: a sprint that cannot start still cancels the crouch
confirmed.where: updatePlayer, sprint-cancels-crouch line (~15703), just above `var sprint=`
confirmed.steps: 1. Sprint away from a pillager by holding Shift+W until stamina hits 0. This sets p.stamLock and p.stamRelease, and sprint is refused until Shift is let go. 2. Keep holding Shift+W, which is normal while fleeing, and press C (or CTRL) to crouch and break the chase. 3. raidKey sets G.crouchTog=true. On the next frame this line clears it again, because it only checks that Shift is held and he is moving. It never checks whether a sprint can actually start. The sprint line below then refuses the sprint anyway. Result: he keeps jogging at full height with no sprint. He never crouches, the 170 hide rule never applies, no HIDDEN plate appears and there is no message. The key looks broken exactly when he needs it to break the chase. The same thing happens when aiming (RMB) or wading, where sprint is also cancelled: pressing Shift while crouched stands him up, and he does not sprint.
confirmed.test: Inside the game closure, in a live raid: clear keys, then set p.stam=0, p.stamLock=1, p.stamRelease=1, keys.ShiftLeft=true, keys.KeyW=true, G.crouchTog=true. Call updatePlayer(1/60). Assert G.pCrouch===true and G.sprinting===false. The current build gives G.pCrouch false and G.crouchTog false, so it FAILS. Control, same keys with p.stam=100 and stamLock=0 and stamRelease=0: G.crouchTog===false and G.sprinting===true on both builds, so sprint still wins whenever it can start. Restore keys and stamina in finally.

verdict.reason:
I could not refute it. Every step holds in the current code.

1. What stamina does. Line 15767 `if(p.stam<=2){ p.stamLock=1; p.stamRelease=1; }` sets both flags at the end of the frame when stamina runs dry. Line 15697 `if(!_shHeld) p.stamRelease=0;` clears the release flag only after Shift is let go.

2. What C does. In raidKey, line 11084 `G.crouchTog=!G.crouchTog;` turns crouch on. It runs only on a fresh key press and does not check Shift.

3. The cancel line. On the next frame, line 15703 `if(_shHeld&&mg>0&&G.crouchTog&&!p.downed){ G.crouchTog=false; crouch=false; }` turns crouch off again. It checks only that Shift is held and he is moving. The sprint line below it, 15704 `var sprint=_shHeld&&p.stam>2&&!p.stamLock&&!p.stamRelease&&!crouch&&mg>0;`, then refuses the sprint because of the stamina flags. After that, 15712 `if(p.ads) sprint=false;` and 15723 `if(wading) sprint=false;` also refuse sprint after crouch is already gone. Result: he walks at normal speed, standing, with no sprint and no message.

4. This is not deliberate. The v11.53 comment above the line quotes his note, "activating sprint should automatically stop crouching". It also says movement is required, "the same rule sprint itself has". So the line is meant to follow sprint's own rules and just misses the stamina, aiming and wading checks. In these cases no sprint starts, so his note does not apply. No ruling says Shift alone should stand him up.

5. The proposed fix is sound. p.ads is a lasting flag set by the right mouse button (line 11313) and the controller (line 12043), so it is already correct at line 15703. inWaterDeep (line 8215) only reads the map and changes nothing, so calling it here is safe. The fix also uses the same wading edge as line 15722. The stim still works, because the stim (line 15760) keeps stamina at 100 and never sets the locks. No numbers change, so this is not balance.

confirmed.title: Ctrl+mouse wheel to resize the HUD toggles crouch with every Ctrl press
confirmed.where: raidKey crouch toggle (~11083) and the canvas wheel listener (~11258)
confirmed.steps: 1. In a raid, standing, hold Ctrl and roll the wheel. This is his v9.95 HUD-size gesture, and it is also every browser's zoom gesture. 2. The Ctrl keydown goes through raidKey first, which flips G.crouchTog. Crouch has been a toggle since v10.07, so letting go of Ctrl does not undo it. 3. The HUD resizes and he is now crouched at 0.52 speed with the HIDDEN plate up, without having asked to crouch. If he was already crouched to hide, resizing the HUD stands him up and drops the 170 hide rule. Neither case shows a message.
confirmed.test: Inside the closure, in a raid: note P.uiScale and set G.crouchTog=false. Dispatch keydown ControlLeft on window only. Dispatch a cancelable WheelEvent on cv with ctrlKey:true and deltaY:-100. Dispatch keyup ControlLeft. Step one frame. Assert that P.uiScale changed (the resize ran), and that G.crouchTog===false and G.pCrouch===false. The current build leaves crouchTog true, so it FAILS. Control: keydown and keyup ControlLeft with no wheel leaves crouchTog===true on both builds, so plain Ctrl still crouches. Pad RS click is unaffected because its key is cleared in the same frame. In finally, restore P.uiScale, call applyMenuZoom() and saveProfile().

verdict.reason:
Confirmed from the current code. In a raid the keydown listener ends with `raidKey(e.code,e.repeat,e);`. On the first, non-repeat Ctrl press, raidKey runs `if((code==='ControlLeft'||code==='ControlRight'||code==='KeyC')&&G&&!G.over&&!G.sim&&!repeat){ G.crouchTog=!G.crouchTog; }`. Nothing in that branch checks whether a wheel follows. The only keyup handler is `window.addEventListener('keyup',function(e){ keys[e.code]=false; });`, so letting go of Ctrl leaves the stance flipped. The canvas wheel listener then runs `if(e.ctrlKey){ if(e.deltaY!==0) hudSizeStep(e.deltaY<0?1:-1); return; }`, which resizes the HUD and does not touch crouch. The change is real: `crouchHeld(){ return !!(G&&G.crouchTog); }` feeds `var crouch=crouchHeld();` in updatePlayer, which sets movement, sprint and hiding. The only message is hudSizeStep's `say('HUD size N%')`. Nothing says crouch changed. The two features come from two separate notes of his: v9.92 made Ctrl or C crouch, and v9.95 made Ctrl+wheel size the HUD. v10.07 then made crouch a toggle. No comment or ruling mentions the clash; a grep for ctrl-wheel near crouch finds nothing. This is an input bug, not balance.

The proposed fix is on the right track, but it has two problems. (1) G.ctrlCrouch is never cleared when Ctrl is released, so a value left over from an earlier press stays around. Example: a Ctrl press while the pause box is up sets `keys[code]=true`, then `return`s at the pauseOpen line before the crouch flip. A later Ctrl+wheel then undoes a flip this press never made. (2) It undoes the press by flipping again, not by restoring the old stance. Holding Ctrl and then rolling (`G.crouchTog=false; // v11.53`) or sprinting (`if(_shHeld&&mg>0&&G.crouchTog&&!p.downed){ G.crouchTog=false; ...}`) before the wheel makes that second flip crouch him again. Restoring the stance from before the press avoids both problems. It also keeps his v13.36 rule "one change per click" on the press. The `keys` check stays so that a trackpad pinch, which sends ctrlKey wheel events with no Ctrl keydown, changes nothing. One gap remains: he is crouched for the few frames between the Ctrl press and the first wheel notch. That cannot be avoided without moving the crouch to key release, which would change when crouch happens.

confirmed.title: The crouch state is frozen for the whole bleed-out (and through a roll): crouched when downed means pillagers past 170 cannot see or shoot the body
confirmed.where: damagePlayer going-down line (~13106), tryRoll (~12304). G.pCrouch is written only at the bottom of updatePlayer (~15829), below the downed and roll early returns
confirmed.steps: 1. Crouch behind cover. A pillager finds him inside 170 and downs him. 2. updatePlayer returns early in the downed branch every frame, so G.pCrouch (and G.pBush and G.pConceal) keep the values from his last standing frame for up to 17 seconds. 3. The hard crouch rule in updateEnts reads G.pCrouch, so every hostile pillager further than 170 has sees=false. His acqT never builds and he never fires at the body, while each hit on a downed player should cost 3 seconds of bleed. A player downed while standing at the same spot is shot as intended; machines already ignore a downed player by a separate rule that deliberately leaves pillagers able to see. Under the red wash the plate reads HIDDEN · CROUCHED while the body is lying down. Pressing C on the floor flips crouchTog with no effect. After a revive he gets up in whatever stance that flip left. The roll does the same for 0.38s: tryRoll clears the toggle, but G.pCrouch stays true until the roll ends, so a roll out of crouch keeps him hidden past 170 and shows the HIDDEN plate while the status reads ROLLING, although a roll is supposed to leave the crouch.
confirmed.test: Inside the closure, at seed 4242: set G.ents to a single hostile, non-hire pillager (hostile=true, state 'chase', cd 0, acqT 0) 200 units from the player with a clear line of sight, facing him. At 200 he is past the 170 rule and inside the 242 no-throw edge. Arm A: G.crouchTog=true, run updatePlayer(1/60) once, set p.iv=0, call damagePlayer(999,'test','TEST'), then run updatePlayer and updateEnts at 1/60 for 90 frames and record p.downT and the pillager's acqT. Arm B (control): the same, with crouchTog=false before the down. Current build: in arm A acqT stays 0 and downT falls only by time (about 15.5), while in arm B he acquires and fires (downT falls by at least 3 more). Fixed build: the two arms match. Restore G.ents and the player in finally.

verdict.reason:
I tried to refute this and couldn't. Every step checks out in the current code.

1. Nothing updates the crouch flag while he is down or rolling. There are only two lines that write G.pCrouch. One is the bot's `G.pCrouch=!!botCrouch;` in updateBot. The other is `G.pCrouch=!!crouch;` at the bottom of updatePlayer. Both early returns in updatePlayer come before that line: the downed branch `if(p.downed){ ... tryExtractTick(dt,!!keys['KeyE']); return; }` and the roll branch `if(p.roll>0){ ... tryExtractTick(dt); return; }`.
2. Going down does not clear it either. The going-down line is `p.hp=0; p.downed=true; p.downT=CFG.downTime; p.pendKiller=src; p.prep=null; p.prepA=null;`, and neither it, tickDowned, giveUpTick nor selfRevive touches G.crouchTog or G.pCrouch. The C key handler `G.crouchTog=!G.crouchTog;` has no downed guard.
3. Pillagers past 170 lose sight of the body. In updateEnts, `if(sees&&G.pCrouch&&!WDC&&CHID>0&&!onYou&&dist(e,p)>CHID&&(!G.sim||HARDC)) sees=false;` runs every frame. By default crouchBreaksChase is 1, so onYou is false. The very next line, `if(sees&&p.downed&&e.kind!=='raider') sees=false;`, blinds only machines, so pillagers are meant to keep seeing a downed man.
4. So they never shoot him. The pillager chase branch builds `e.acqT=sees?((e.acqT||0)+dt):0;` and fires only under `if(e.cd<=0&&sees&&d<e.rng&&e.acqT>=...)`, with no p.downed check. A hit on a downed player goes to `p.downT-=3;` in damagePlayer. A stale crouch therefore removes that cost for every pillager past 170.
5. The sim already treats a downed body as not crouched. updateBot guards `if(CRN>0&&!p.downed){` before it sets botCrouch, so the bot is never crouched while down. The live game disagrees with its own sim here.
6. The screen is wrong too. drawHUD has no downed return before `var _cr=!!G.pCrouch`, so the plate shows 'HIDDEN  ·  CROUCHED' while he is lying down.
7. The roll has the same problem. tryRoll's `G.crouchTog=false;   // v11.53, HIS NOTE: "rolling should automatically stop crouching"` leaves G.pCrouch true for the whole roll. The hard crouch rule and the plate keep treating him as crouched for 0.38s, while playerStatus returns 'ROLLING' first.

No nearby comment or ruling says this is deliberate, and it is stale state rather than a balance dial.

The proposed fix is incomplete. G.pConceal was also last computed with crouched=true. concealAt gives 0.10 for crouched and still in a bush, against 0.40 standing, and that value multiplies every sight range through `_fSee=...*pcon`. So a body downed while crouched in a bush would still be almost invisible after the proposed fix, and the gap it describes against a man downed standing would remain. G.pBush also goes stale while he crawls. The corrected fix below refreshes all three every frame in the downed branch, the way updateBot does.
verdict.correctedFix:
1) In damagePlayer, the going-down line:
p.hp=0; p.downed=true; p.downT=CFG.downTime; p.pendKiller=src; p.prep=null; p.prepA=null; G.crouchTog=false; G.pCrouch=false;

2) In the downed branch of updatePlayer, directly after the crawl line
    if(mg0>0){ p.x+=(mx0/mg0)*30*dt; p.y+=(my0/mg0)*30*dt; collide(p,G.map.walls); }
insert:
    G.pBush=inBush(p.x,p.y); G.pCrouch=false; G.pConceal=concealAt(p.x,p.y,mg0>0,false,false);   // a man on the floor is not crouching; updateBot's downed frames already read it this way

3) In tryRoll:
  G.crouchTog=false; G.pCrouch=false; G.pConceal=concealAt(p.x,p.y,true,false,false);   // v11.53, HIS NOTE: "rolling should automatically stop crouching"

These lines draw no seeded values, change no text and move no dial.

confirmed.title: Red noise marks for unseen sounds are drawn under the darkness and fog-of-war sheets, so they are buried exactly where they are shown
confirmed.where: world pass of the renderer (~23966), drawn before the lighting overlay (~24020) and the fog blit `wc.drawImage(fogC,0,0);` (~24238)
confirmed.steps: noiseMark only keeps sounds whose position canSee() says he cannot see, which is always ground under the fog-of-war sheet. The ring is painted there, and then the night sheet (0.30) and the fog sheet (about 0.46 by day, 0.60 by night) are laid over it. At night the ring reaches the screen at roughly 28 percent of its alpha. This is the v4.05 fault that ringsOnTop fixed for G.pings, repeated for the v9.07 marks. Gunshots also get a ping ring on top, but some sounds have only this mark: the charge warning where a pillager's grenade lands (v15.28), the Listener and Crier windups, and the extraction inbound, touchdown and last-call sounds. At night a grenade landing out of sight behind him shows as a faint smudge.
confirmed.test: Inside the closure, at night in clear weather at 1920x1080 with DPR pinned and __topClear first: put a spot 300 units directly behind the player. Draw one frame with G.noiseRings=[{x,y,t:0.35,life:1.15,r:60,a0:0.65}] and one with G.noiseRings=[]. Take the largest rise of red minus blue in a 3px band at the ring radius (world to screen). Assert a rise of at least 60. Current build: roughly 15 or less, so it FAILS. Control at the same spot: a G.pings entry {src:'robot',typ:'fire',s:500,occ:1,t:0.3,life:1.1} is drawn by the ringsOnTop pass and shows a large rise on both builds, which proves the probe can see a ring there.

verdict.reason: I could not refute it. Every step checks out in the current code. (1) The block the auditor quoted is at line 23966, `if(G.noiseRings) for(i=0;i<G.noiseRings.length;i++){`, inside the world transform that opens at line 22621 with `wc.save(); wc.scale(Z,Z); wc.translate(-ox,-oy);` and closes at line 24011 with `wc.restore();`. (2) After that pass, line 24096 draws the darkness layer with `wc.drawImage(litC,0,0);`. Its fill is set at lines 24032-24033 (NIGHT_SHEET by night). Line 24238 then draws the fog layer with `wc.drawImage(fogC,0,0);`. Its fill is set at lines 24209 and 24220: `clamp(.46-...)` by day and `clamp(.60-...)` by night. So the marks sit under both layers. (3) noiseMark (lines 3827-3845) returns early on `if(canSee(p.x,p.y,p.face,wx,wy,G.vseg)) return;`. So a mark only exists where he cannot see, which is the fogged area. The one exception is the small cutout around him at line 24237 (`fx2.arc(psx,psy,AMBR(),...)`), which does not change the overall claim. (4) The v4.05 comment at lines 24255-24263 names this exact fault for pings ("the rings were being buried exactly where they mattered"). Its fix, `if(CFG.ringsOnTop!==0){`, covers only G.pings. The v9.07 block's own comment gives world-space placement as its only reason, and nothing marks drawing under the fog as deliberate. CFG shows `noiseSee:1`, so the marks are on. (5) This is draw order only; no gameplay numbers change, so it is not balance. The proposed fix is correct. At the insertion point after the pings block's `wc.restore(); }` at line 24303, the canvas is back in plain source-over drawing, because line 24169 runs `wc.globalAlpha=1; wc.globalCompositeOperation='source-over';`. The fix uses the same save, scale and translate as the world pass at line 22621. `i` is a var shared across the function, and `var nr`/`nf` are declared inside the moved block, so moving it breaks nothing. One optional refinement: to match the ringsOnTop dial, the fix could also keep the old block in the world pass behind `if(CFG.ringsOnTop===0)` and put `CFG.ringsOnTop!==0&&` in front of the new block. The fix is valid without it.

confirmed.title: Dragging a backpack stack and letting go back on its own cell moves one item out
confirmed.where: invCell, the cell.onclick guard (about line 32065), together with the pointer-drag mouseup listener after grabbable (about line 34989)
confirmed.steps:
1. On the Stash screen, pack two Medkits so the Backpack shows Medkit x2.
2. Press on the Medkit cell and drag it toward the stash. The ghost follows the cursor.
3. Change your mind, bring it back and let go on the same Medkit cell.

What goes wrong: the backpack drop for from 'kit' does nothing, which is correct. But the guard that should throw away the click after a drag never fires. The document mouseup runs grabEnd(), which sets GRAB=null, before the browser sends the click. That click reaches the cell and runs opt.act(1), so the backpack now shows Medkit x1 and one Medkit went home with no message. The same happens on the ascent check. There a kit cell drag-and-return puts one back, and a stash cell drag-and-return packs one ('click: carry one').
confirmed.test:
Inside the closure, at 1920x1080 with __topClear:
- Set P.stash=['medkit','medkit'], P.kit=['medkit','medkit'], P.hotAssign={}, P.freeKit=0. Put 'on' on #hub and call renderHub().
- Take c = the first '#kitgrid .cell:not(.slotempty)' and its centre (x,y).
- Dispatch on c: mousedown (button 0, bubbles, cancelable, clientX x, clientY y).
- Dispatch on document: mousemove to a point inside #stashgrid, then mousemove back to (x,y).
- Dispatch on c: mouseup (button 0, bubbles) at (x,y), then click (bubbles, detail 1).
- Assert packedCount('medkit')===2. The current build gives 1.

verdict.reason:
I could not refute either case. Both hold in the current code.

The dropzone on each stash-screen belt cell (renderHub, hotplanwrap) has two branches before the quoted line. The first is the v14.17 same-cell guard `if(from==='plan:'+ix){ ... return; }`. The second is `var why=(from==='rack')?rackPut(ix,key):planPut(ix,key);`. A key dragged from another key carries `from='plan:N'` (from `grabbable(el,_pk,'plan:'+ix,ITEMS[_pk].name);`), so it always goes to planPut.

Case A: planPut runs `for(var ok in P.hotAssign) if(P.hotAssign[ok]===key) delete P.hotAssign[ok]; P.hotAssign[slot]=key;`. It never reads what the target key held, so the Frag's binding is simply overwritten. The Frag stays in P.kit and shows again in the backpack grid, because the backpack hides one copy per binding. Key 3 is left empty. That is exactly the behaviour the v14.25 comment in the floor-backpack mouseup calls a bug: "dragging key 3 onto a filled key 4 deleted what key 4 held instead of swapping it back onto key 3. The raid drop has done both since v8.04". The floor backpack now swaps with `if(d.fromHot!==undefined&&_hPrev&&_hPrev!==d.key) G.hotAssign[d.fromHot]=_hPrev;`, and so does the raid drop (`G.hotAssign[d.fromHot]=_prevHot`). No comment near the stash belt says an overwrite is intended.

Case B: the armoury row drags with `grabbable(oc,_ik,'rack',W.name)`. For a gun in his hands, rackToStash returns null at `if(P.equipped===gk||P.equippedSec===gk) return null;`, so the gun never enters P.stash, and rackPut binds the key alone. Equipped guns are always in P.weapons (see the Equip path, which pushes to P.weapons). Dragging that key to another key reaches planPut, which counts only P.stash (`if(P.stash[i]===key) held++`). With no spare it returns 'That is not in your stash any more.', which the dropzone says with a clank. With a spare gun_smg in the stash, held is 1 and picked is 0, so `P.kit.push(key)` packs the spare without being asked. dropDeadKeys (v14.85) already counts the two equipped guns as live keys, so a key on an in-hand gun is a supported state.

The ascent check belt (renderStage) does not register its cells as drag sources, so a `plan:` drag cannot happen there, and the fix belongs only in renderHub.

The proposed fix is sound. `_fk` is never equal to ix, because the v14.17 guard returns first. Sending in-hand guns through rackPut binds the key without packing and passes rackToStash's armoury check. The swap runs only after a successful put. The put has already deleted `_fk`, so writing `_was` back to `_fk` gives the same swap as v14.25 and v8.04. It adds no player text and changes no numbers.

refuted.title: The key list does not close on ESC or TAB: they open the pause box over it and it stays up
refuted.reason:
The quoted code exists and the key path works as described: backOut() (the Tab branch ahead of the floor code) has no legend entry, `var _hubBusy=...` leaves out HB.legend, and `if((code==='Escape'||code==='KeyP'||code==='Tab')&&!repeat&&G&&!G.over)` pauses whatever G.legendOn is. But this is designed behaviour, not a fault.

(1) Both key lists are HUD overlays, not menus. The raid list is the H cycle `if(code==='KeyH'&&G&&!repeat) G.legendOn=(G.legendOn+1)%3;`. The raid runs underneath it, its footer says `ctx.fillText('H  hide',...)`, and his 2026-09-03 answers list the legend under HUD (Q25, Q27: shown by default). His "ESC closes every menu" answer (Q1) covers menu screens.

(2) The floor CONTROLS box also runs as an overlay: _hubBusy ignores it, so you can walk and use stations with it up. Its own lines are `'TAB','pause, or back out' ... 'H','close this'`, so TAB pausing and only H closing it is exactly what the box says. The raid list's own row also says `['TAB','pause, or back out of a menu']`, and the key list is not a menu.

(3) The NEW IN card is meant to be dismissed by walking or ENTER. Its comment reads "Dismissed by walking, because the first thing anybody does on the hub is walk", and it draws `'press ENTER or walk to dismiss'`. After a pause, walking still clears it.

(4) The proposed floor fix is also wrong. It does not check pauseOpen, and `if(pauseOpen&&e.code!=='KeyP'&&e.code!=='Escape'&&e.code!=='Tab'){...}` lets ESC and TAB through while the box is up. So with CONTROLS up, press P to pause, then ESC or TAB: the fix hides the CONTROLS box behind the pause box and leaves the pause box open. That breaks the v13.44 rule that the pause box, being in front, closes first. Changing what ESC and TAB do over a HUD panel would need his ruling, not a bug fix.

refuted.title: Controller B does nothing at the Peddler stall
refuted.reason: The mechanics are right: B does nothing at the stall. The finding calls that a broken rule, and the code shows no such rule. (1) The quoted lines exist in pollPad's `if(G.trade&&!G.over){` branch. It reads only D-UP/D-DOWN (12/13), A (0), X (2) and Menu (9), stamps PAD.prev and returns. padOpenModal finds no panel, because drawTrade paints the stall on the canvas. So pad B is inert there. (2) This is deliberate scoping. The v13.49 comment lists the stall's pad controls ("X walks away, the button the stall prompt names. Nothing else on the pad acts behind the panel"). With a pad on, drawTrade prints `'['+keyLabel('KeyE','E')+'] walk away'`, which reads [X]. He is never stuck. (3) The keyboard comparison is wrong. In the raid, pad B is PADTAP `1:'Space'`, the roll. The stall's raidKey branch deliberately swallows that key: `if(code==='KeyG'||code==='Space'||code==='KeyQ'||code==='KeyC') return;`. So pad B already matches its keyboard key. Keyboard B closes the stall only because B is the backpack key: `if(code==='Escape'||code==='KeyE'||code==='Tab'||code==='KeyI'||code==='KeyB'){ G.trade=null; ...}`. His v13.45 ruling says "B NO LONGER BACKS OUT", and TAB has the back-out. (4) There is no pad rule that B closes a menu painted on the canvas during a raid. With the raid map or backpack open, pad B still goes through the PADTAP loop to `if(code==='Space'&&G&&!G.over&&!G.paused&&!repeat) tryRoll();`. It rolls and closes nothing. B backs out only of DOM panels, through padMenu. So the premise that "only the pad breaks his rule that B closes every menu" is false. What remains is a suggestion to make pad controls consistent, not a defect. (If it were ever wanted, the proposed line is safe: the stamp loop that follows sets PAD.prev[1], so the same held B would not roll on the next poll.)
